intro_html: Posole verde is a hearty green Mexican stew, and this version leans on tomatillos and poblanos for a bright, mildly spicy broth. Built on hominy with 56 grams of protein a bowl, it runs about $3.72 a serving (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings means a big pot of soul-warming stew ready whenever you are.
cost_closing_html: About $3.72 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving runs about 562 calories with 56 grams of protein.
upsell_html: A warm bowl of this on a cold day is worth every minute the slow cooker spent on it. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Canned hominy is the heart of posole and it is cheap. Grab a few cans, since it doubles as both starch and body for the stew.
Tomatillos and poblanos are usually tucked in the Mexican produce section and cost a lot less than you would guess. Look there first.
This stew reheats beautifully, so freeze half the batch if fourteen servings is more than a week's worth for you.
make_it: Set the pork loin in the slow cooker with the chopped onion.
Add the tomatillos, poblano peppers, and enough water to nearly cover.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork is tender.
Shred the pork right in the pot and stir it back through the broth.
Stir in the drained hominy and cook another 20 to 30 minutes to warm through.
Ladle into bowls, hominy and all, and portion into containers.
